findings.title: Deleting a data object leaves its retained data association semantically orphaned
findings.why_it_matters: The delete cascade only recognizes SequenceFlow, MessageFlow, and Association as connection objects that must be removed when an endpoint is deleted. A valid retained BPMN DataOutputAssociation/DataInputAssociation is outside the typed API, so deleting a supported DataObjectReference only clears its required endpoint reference and keeps the association. bpmn-moddle accepts the resulting XML without a parser warning, so the post-serialization atomicity check also accepts and autosaves a semantically broken process; repeated export/save cannot repair it.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify all retained relationship objects whose required source/target reference points to a deleted semantic (including bpmn:DataInputAssociation and bpmn:DataOutputAssociation) as dependents to detach, rather than clearing the endpoint. Complement the unresolved-reference parser check with required-reference/semantic validation for the retained moddle graph, and add deletion cases for data associations and other non-API moddle relationships.
evidence: Constructed warning-free BPMN: add `bpmn:dataObjectReference id="DataObjectRef_Delete"` to the fixture and add `<bpmn:dataOutputAssociation id="OutputAssoc_Delete"><bpmn:targetRef>DataObjectRef_Delete</bpmn:targetRef></bpmn:dataOutputAssociation>` inside Task_Unrelated. bpmn-moddle parses it with no warnings and resolves targetRef to DataObjectRef_Delete.

After import, `DataObjectRef_Delete` is a managed typed element. Calling deleteElement on it succeeds; export then reports `data false association true target undefined warnings []`. A subsequent save also succeeds, proving the malformed relationship is persisted and not just an in-memory intermediate.

detachSemantic handles a scalar retained reference by recursively detaching only BPMNShape/BPMNEdge or the three types recognized by isBpmnConnectionType; every other owner, including bpmn:DataOutputAssociation, falls through to `owner[property.name] = undefined` (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:550-564).

serializeRetained validates only parser warnings and unresolved IDs after writing XML (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:529-539). The targetRef omission creates neither condition, so commitMutation writes the invalid semantic state and publishes it atomically to memory and disk.

residual_risks: Verified resolved: a valid Association with an unindexed Lane imports and survives an unrelated update; deleting Task_Unrelated removes its Lane reference and all shapes in a secondary BPMNDiagram; the resulting document can be saved again.
Verified resolved: repeated create/connect/export/save/delete/export of a newly added task leaves no warnings or orphaned typed flow, and a failed unsafe saveAs leaves the active filename unchanged.

Arbitrary extension-namespace attributes may encode opaque ID strings that bpmn-moddle cannot describe as references. A safe deletion policy must define whether to preserve such opaque values or reject a deletion that could affect them.
testing_gaps: Add focused import-roundtrip fixtures for DataInputAssociation and DataOutputAssociation whose referenced DataObjectReference is deleted; assert the association is removed rather than serialized without a required endpoint, then reopen and mutate/save again.

Inventory valid BPMN relationship types outside BPMN_CONNECTION_TYPES and test deletion through their scalar and collection reference properties (for example data associations and event/data references).
Add an atomicity regression that makes post-serialization semantic validation fail, then asserts both the autosaved file and active context remain byte/canonically unchanged.
